To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the collective dynamics of a population of IF neurons can be described by an equation for the mean spike rate nu(t), which is stable in the asynchronous state if the slope of the static current-to-rate transfer curve of the single neuron is positive; finite-size effects, which are taken into account by a stochastic extension to the mean-field theory, act as a self-stimulation, probing the spectrum of the collective activity in the frequency range from a few Hz to very high frequency (determined by the spike transmission

the collective activity of the population of IF neurons is stable, provided that the slope of the static, current-to-spike rate transfer function is larger than a critical value, and that the characteristic times of the transient collective response of the population are determined by a diffusion process.

the collective activity of a homogeneous network is stable if the slope of the single neuron, current-to-rate, transfer function is positive, and that finite-size fluctuations of the collective activity of an asynchronous network act as an ongoing, self-stimulation, probing the spectral structure of its dynamics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamical properties of a population of neurons in the framework of the integrate and fire model.
the population dynamics of a homogeneous network, where the activity depends both on the field and on fluctuations.
the population dynamics of spiking neurons in a homogeneous network; we derive dynamical equations for the mean and variance of the population activity, and study their properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the population dynamics of spiking neurons can be understood and predicted in the framework of the dynamical equations derived in this work.

the collective activity of a finite-size neural network of IF neurons in an asynchronous regime is a stochastic process whose spectral structure is determined by the single neuron static transfer function, and by the finite-size fluctuations.
the population dynamics is a complex process that can be described by a simple dynamical equation, provided that the network is sufficiently homogeneous.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have derived a simple dynamical equation for spike emission rate nu of a homogeneous network with finite size.
the population dynamics of IF neurons can be described by a diffusion process, whose characteristic times depend on the single cell transfer function.
the collective dynamics of a network of spiking neurons is a dynamical process with a characteristic time which depends on the slope of a neuron transfer function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the population dynamics is described in terms of a dynamical equation for nu(t) that depends on both the mean afferents and on the fluctuations, which are described by a diffusion process.
a dynamical equation for nu can be derived for a network of IF neuron, and that the local stability conditions are expressed in terms of the slope of the single neuron, transfer function.
the dynamical properties of a network of interacting IF neurons are governed by a few simple parameters, the static properties of the single neuron.
